summary: Lackawanna District fire tower blown down in a November 1950 windstorm; its Tark Hill replacement was reported open in April 1952 and was dismantled by 1960.

facts.status_note: Blown down in a windstorm in November 1950; the Tark Hill tower that replaced it was later dismantled.

events.note: Steel Aermotor tower, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association register
Blown down by heavy winds in November 1950
Struck from the Lackawanna District's official list of fire towers in early April 1951
Tark Hill tower on Suscon Road, about five miles from Dupont, reported open in April 1952 to replace it

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register spells it Big Shiney; the 1951 and 1952 newspapers, as transcribed, wrote Big Shinney and Big Shinny. The record keeps Big Shinney.

notes_for_editor: The built year (1928) and steel Aermotor design rest on the register alone. The 1950 destruction date is consistent across three sources. The Tark Hill tower has its own Forest Lookouts page and is not in the queue; it may merit a separate record. The 1960 replacement south of Dupont is only traced to one 1960 newspaper report. Forest Lookouts quotes Scranton, Pittston, Times Leader and Wilkes-Barre papers; the originals were not read. A North Pocono Historical Society Facebook post appeared in search results but could not be read, so none of its claims are used. No photos added.
